questions.question: In 2022, what time did Chahat Arora wrap up the 100 m breaststroke race at the FINA World Swimming Championships in Melbourne, Australia?
questions.solution:

• At the **FINA World Swimming Championships 2022 **in **Melbourne, Australia,** Indian swimmer **Chahat Arora** made headlines by establishing a national record in the women’s **100-meter breaststroke **event. 
 
• Clocking in at **1 minute and 13.13 seconds, **Arora's performance showcased her prowess in the pool. 
 
• However, Lithuania’s Ruta Meilutyte surged ahead in the overall heats with a remarkable time of 1 minute and 3.81 seconds, outpacing Arora by 9.32 seconds. 
 
• South Africa's 19-year-old Lara Van Niekerk secured second place with a time of 1 minute and 3.93 seconds, while Lilly King from the USA claimed the third spot, finishing in 1 minute and 3.94 seconds. 
 
• Looking ahead, Arora is set to participate in the women’s 50-meter breaststroke event, while Siva Sridhar will represent India in the 100-meter individual medley.

• Operating as an international non-governmental organization headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, FINA was established on July 19, 1908, in London by eight founding entities, including British Swimming, the Hungarian Swimming Association, and the Fédération Française de Natation.
 
• Affiliated with the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations, FINA holds recognition from the International Olympic Committee for its role in overseeing international competitions within aquatic sports disciplines.

questions.question: Which award is given to the best coach in sports and games?

options.text: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Dronacharya award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dronacharya award **is associated with **Sports.**

 
 
• It is awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.**
 
• It is **awarded to the Coaches** for their achievement in producing** "Outstanding Sportsperson".**
 
• It was first awarded in 1985 to **Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat.**
 
• The reward amount for this Prize is **₹ 15 lakh.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• Arjun** Award **

 
 
• It was started in 1961 by the government of India. 
 
• Ministry of Youth Affairs and sports awards best sportspersons. 
 
• Those who have shown constantly good performance for 4 years at the international level will be chosen for this award. 
 
• The Awardee will be awarded a cash prize worth Rs. 15 lakh and a bronze statue. 
 
• Krishna Das was the first person to be awarded the Arjun Award in 1984.
 
 
 
• The** Dhyanchand Award **has been constituted by the** Government of India in 2002** to honour lifetime achievement in sports and games.
 
 
• Dhyan Chand was a celebrated **hockey player of India,** mainly before independence.
 
• He won three gold medals with the Indian Team in the Olympics of** 1928, 1932, and 1936.**
 
 
 
• The **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award,** which will now be referred to as the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, recognises sportspersons who have excelled at the international level over a period of four years. It carries a cash reward of **Rs 25 lakh**
 
• This award in Sports is the highest sporting honor of India.
 
 
• It is awarded by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. **
 
• The first recipient of the award was **Viswanathan Anand**, who was the country's **first chess Grandmaster.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Arjuna Award has been enhanced to **15 lakh rupees from 5 lakh**. The Dhronacharya (Lifetime) awardees, who were earlier given 5 lakh rupees will now be given 15 lakh rupees as cash prizes, while Dhronacharya (Regular) will be given 10 lakh instead of 5 lakh rupees per awardee. Dhyanchand Awardees will be given **10 lakh rupees instead of 5 lakh rupees. **
 
• The prize money for the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award has been increased to 25 lakh rupees** from the previous amount of 7.5 lakh rupees.

questions.question: Where did India win its last Olympic medal in men’s hockey? (As of March, 2024).

• The medal win at Tokyo 2020 was India's **12th Olympic medal** in men’s hockey.

• The Games are considered the world's foremost sports competition and are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every four years but two years apart.
 
 
 
• **Men's Field Hockey**
 
 
• Field hockey is a team sport of the hockey family, which is played on grass, watered turf, artificial turf, or synthetic field, as well as an indoor boarded surface.
 
• India has a rich history in men's field hockey, having won numerous medals in past Olympic Games, including eight gold medals.
 
 
 
• **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**
 
 
• The Tokyo 2020 Olympics were originally scheduled to take place in 2020 but were postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• This edition of the Olympics saw significant safety protocols and restrictions due to the ongoing pandemic.

• He holds various cricket records including the only player to have scored one hundred international centuries, the first batsman to score a double century in a One Day International, and the only player to complete more than 34,000 runs in both ODI and Test cricket.
 
• Calls have been made over the years to award Major Dhyan Chand with Bharat Ratna, the country’s highest civilian award. But never happened.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India.
 
• The Bharat Ratna was introduced on 2 January 1954.
 
• It is awarded in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor. 
 
• The number of annual awards is restricted to a maximum of three in a particular year. 
 
• On conferment of the award, the recipient receives a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a medallion.
 
• The first recipients of the Bharat Ratna who were honored in 1954 are as follows:
 
 
• C. Rajagopalachari - The last Governor-General of the Dominion of India 
 
• Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan - Second President and the First Vice President of India
 
• C. V. Raman - Nobel Prize Laureate, Physicist
